title: Linn — Skerries & Storm-Oaths
label: chap:linn

overview.tagline: The sea keeps better counsel than any scribe, and the frost remembers every oath sworn upon its winds — but the Temple of Light arrives with ink and fire to rewrite what the ice has carved.
overview.genre: Norse coastal saga. Oath-driven honor, the tyranny of the season, and one specific terror: the deed nobody saw.
overview.starting_location: A longship house lined with storm-charms and whale-bone runes, salt wind clawing at the doors. A Net-Wife binds a storm-token into a PC's palm. 'The Whale-Road sings,' she says. 'But the Mistlands whistle back. Bring us three keel-lengths of ironwood from the Valewood edge, or the tide will take our boats in the spring. The frost remembers the shelter you took last winter. Pay, or the ice will hold it against you.'

lore.history: North of the Aberderrin Sea, where fjords split the coast and skerries break the tide, dwell the Linn. They are traders and raiders in equal breath, their longships crowding the whale-road and river mouths. They descend the Ylolka like an axe-blade and cut into southern shores, or slip through the Thin Strip where the Valewood dares not touch salt. Yet even these storm-oath people dread the Mistlands and the Valewood, whose fog and trees have no need of ships or harbors to claim their due. The Linn measure their lives in seasons, not years: a season for raiding (summer), a season for planting (spring), a season for governance (autumn, when the Thing meets), and a season for survival (winter, when the frost sets its mark). The winter debt is not a book — it is a set of carved oath-sticks, each notch a promise kept or broken. When a Linn says a debt is 'written in frost,' they mean it is unchangeable until the ice melts. And the ice, in the high north, never truly melts. The gods of the Linn are not distant. Adar, the All-Father, walks the ridges in a gray cloak, his one eye watching for those who break oaths — god of wisdom, death, and binding promises. Rorg, the Storm Father, rides the clouds, his hammer cracking the sky, patron of raiders and sailors. His cult is loud, proud, and dangerous. The Temple of Light calls him a demon. The Linn call him captain.
lore.first_notice: The smell of tar and salt fish. The creak of oars from unseen boats. The way everyone — jarl to thrall — touches a knotted cord before speaking of the sea. The oath-sticks hanging from every belt, each mark a weight carried.
lore.rule_that_kills: Never name a drowned person aloud while underway. The sea collects names, and if it hears you speaking one it doesn't recognize, it may reach up to correct the debt. Also, never refuse a cup of winter mead — it is a test of your honor and your weight.

entanglements.southeast: Valewood (via the Thin Coast) — the portage across the Thin Coast brings iron and amber; the trees watch the passage. The portage is a treaty, not a road.
entanglements.west: Mistlands (via the Aberderrin Sea) — the fog-bells and sea-roads are respected; a Linn raider knows which bell means 'welcome' and which means 'trap.' The fog is a better ally than any flag.
entanglements.farSouth: The Dolmis Sea — Zakov and Aelinnel are destinations for trade and plunder; the tides are a better map than any chart. The sea-queen's words carry across the water.
entanglements.farWest: The Aberderrin Sea — the ice and the deep currents define the edge of the world; the dead lie beneath the keel. The northern horizon is a silence that listens.

regional_diagnostic.current_hook: The sea keeps better counsel than any scribe, and the frost remembers every oath sworn upon its winds — but the Temple of Light arrives with ink and fire to rewrite what the ice has carved.
regional_diagnostic.core_conflict: Players are caught between the **Jarls' raiding economy**, the **Sea-Queen's coastal law**, and the **Temple of Light's crusade** of re-education and assimilation — each demanding oaths that contradict the others. The Linn fear the Mistlands and the Direwood across the Aberderrin sea, but they also fear the Valewood to their south. The Ninth is the unwitnessed death; the Hollow is the silence of the forgotten.
regional_diagnostic.unique_feature: **Frost-Bound Memory:** Oaths are carved in ice that never fully melts; breaking a storm-oath inflicts mechanical penalties (Fatigue/Harm) and gives the GM free Story Beats representing the sea's attention.
regional_diagnostic.ninth_taboo:
The ninth horn frightens the Linn exactly as much as it frightens anybody else. They are not braver than the Mistlanders or the Aelaerem. They have simply gone the other way about it.

Everywhere else the wise stop at eight. In a Linn longhouse a man calls for the ninth and blows it, and he does it fast, before his nerve can get a word in. The custom exists because nerve fails: the horn is kept by someone other than the man who will blow it, intent is announced out loud in front of the hall so it cannot be quietly reconsidered, and the village turns out so that walking away costs more than going on. None of that is there for ceremony. It is there because men change their minds, and the Linn have built a machine for not letting them.

Men are sick beforehand. This is unremarkable and no one comments. What is remarked on, for the rest of a life, is the man who called for the horn and then did not blow it.

Something comes and stands at the high table when it sounds, and the Linn call it Adar, and it takes its weight. Ask a man who has done it and he will change the subject with no skill at all. The ones who talk about the ninth in a loud voice are, without exception, the ones who have not.
regional_diagnostic.price: **Warmth, years, and safety, spent gladly.** A Linn does not gamble these for power. They spend them for a witness, which is the only currency the Linn treat as real.

faction_triad.goal: Unite scattered strands under one raiding oath
faction_triad.method: Successful raids, wise judgments at Thing-Holm, frost-mark enforcement
faction_triad.why_players_care: Control harbor access, levy ships, offer raid-truces and oar-shares

faction_triad.goal: Maintain coastal law without drawing blade
faction_triad.method: Envoy network, seal-bags, oath-sticks branded with the queen's mark
faction_triad.why_players_care: Grants harbor-marks, escort writs, audience that bends sea-law

faction_triad.goal: Convert Linn to the Lens of the White Flame (re-education & assimilation)
faction_triad.method: Grain fleets, synod courts, bell-tower consecrations, schoolmasters
faction_triad.why_players_care: Cheap grain, legal alternatives to blood-feuds, protection from 'pagan' hazards

quotes.speaker: High Jarl (Elite)
quotes.text: The sea keeps better counsel than any scribe, and the storm remembers every oath sworn upon its winds. But the frost — the frost is the witness. It preserves what the tide would wash away. A promise sworn in winter is owed until the ice melts. And the ice never truly melts.

quotes.speaker: Net-Wife (Commoner)
quotes.text: The water speaks to those who know how to listen — the way it moves tells you if the fish are running, if the weather's turning, or if something's coming that wasn't invited to the feast. My grandmother taught me to read the frost on the oar-blades. That's how I know who will live through the winter and who will feed the seals.

winter_debts_timer.name: Winter Debts
advance_on: A character accepts a Frost Mark (gift or shelter) (+1)
A storm-oath is broken on the water (+2)
A character publicly refuses a cup of mead in winter (+1)
The party ignores a shrine offering or breaks a local taboo (GM spends 1 SB to tick +1)
A jarl's claim is challenged at the Thing (+1)

thresholds.4: The frost-bound memories stir; all oaths made in winter are now binding at +1 DV.
thresholds.8: The Thing convenes to settle the winter debts. The party must defend all oaths they have sworn or be forced into a quest to pay the accumulated weight.

stirrs_table.complication: A draugr rises from the ice, demanding a blood-price. Fulfill an old oath or fight (Cap 2).
A white bear appears at the longhouse door; hospitality is tested. Offer food or be marked as unwelcoming (−1 Position on social rolls for a week).
A skald composes a verse that twists your past deeds; your reputation suffers. Lose 1 Repute or pay 1 Boon to silence the song.
The Sea-Queen's Hand arrives with a writ; you are summoned to her court to answer a complaint. Travel immediately or face a feud.
A fogfall descends; you are lost in the Mistlands. Navigate Desperately; on a Miss, you gain the Condition Fog-Called.
A rival jarl claims your winter shelter was stolen; start a Feud Timer [4] with his clan.
The ninth horn is blown at a feast; the Hollow manifests. Offer a story or lose a memory.
A Temple bell tower is consecrated nearby; all shrine-devout lose 1 die on faith actions until the tower is silenced.

npcs.name: Jarl Skjold
npcs.role: High Jarl of the Southern Fjords
npcs.motivation: Unite the scattered strands under one oath
npcs.quirk: His beard is braided with silver from every ship he has taken. His oath-stick bears notches from three wars.

npcs.name: Volva Hervor
npcs.motivation: Read the tides of fate before they turn
npcs.quirk: She speaks once a year; the rest of the time she listens to the fog. She reads the frost-bound oaths by touch — her fingers are scarred from counting.

npcs.name: Astrid
npcs.motivation: Keep her village safe from the Hollow and the deep
npcs.quirk: She ties a knot for every storm she's survived. Her belt has thirty. She is the keeper of the village oath-sticks.

npcs.name: Brother Halvard
npcs.role: Missionary of the Temple of Light
npcs.motivation: Convert the Linn to the Lens of the White Flame
npcs.quirk: He carries a water-timer to measure the hours of prayer, but the skerries have no hours. His oath-stick is blank — the Linn do not trust him.

npcs.name: Gunnhild
npcs.motivation: Enforce the queen's will without drawing a blade
npcs.quirk: She never draws her sword. The threat is enough. She carries an oath-stick notched with the names of every jarl who tried to cheat the queen.

npcs.name: The Draugr Jarl
npcs.motivation: A dead jarl whose oath was never fulfilled
npcs.quirk: Said to rise from the Thing-Holm when the ninth bell tolls. His oath-stick is frozen — the marks are filled with ice.

npcs.name: Einar Frost-Tongue
npcs.motivation: Keep the memory of weights alive through verse
npcs.quirk: He has never lost a verse duel. His tongue is forked — he can praise and curse in the same breath. His oath-stick is longer than his arm.

places.title: Kelp-Skerry Gut
places.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [STEALTH]
places.description: Narrow channel where oars scrape weed and rock.
places.flavor: Kelp strands like dead men's hair; row silently or the reef listens.
places.mechanical_hook: Passage requires a Stealth or Boating roll (DV 4); a Miss draws the attention of whatever nests among the weed.

places.title: Tide-Shed
places.subtitle: [REPUTATION]
places.description: Longship houses; tar smoke and gulls for sentries.
places.flavor: Each shed holds a keel's ghost; old crews sleep under the floor planks.
places.mechanical_hook: Sheltering here for the night grants +1 die on the next Reputation-related roll with the ship's former crew's kin, if honored properly.

places.title: Wave-Gate Reef
places.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [DEATH]
places.description: Just off a raiding beach; only locals know the cut.
places.flavor: One wrong turn and the wave breaks over you — twice.
places.mechanical_hook: Crossing without a local pilot forces a Desperate Boating roll (DV 5); failure costs 1 Harm and damages the vessel.

places.title: Runestone Causey
places.subtitle: [LEGEND]
places.description: Across tidal flat; names half lost to barnacle.
places.flavor: Touch the stone with your left hand. If it's warm, the ancestors approve.
places.mechanical_hook: A warm stone grants a Boon on the next Lore or social roll invoking ancestry; a cold stone imposes a Condition (Ill-Omened) until cleared by a proper offering.

places.title: Herring-Stairs
places.subtitle: [LABOR]
places.description: Drying racks above cliff path; knives flicker like fish.
places.flavor: Workers sing a counting song — eight verses, never nine.
places.mechanical_hook: Singing the ninth verse ticks the Winter Debts timer by 1; refusing to sing at all marks the singer as an outsider (−1 die on social rolls here).

places.title: Winter Hall
places.subtitle: [COMMUNITY]
places.description: Turf walls, smoke-eye roof, benches crowded with shields.
places.flavor: The fire never goes out. Feed it a story each night or it goes hungry.
places.mechanical_hook: Telling a genuine story clears 1 Fatigue for the teller and grants +1 die to the next social roll in the hall; refusing three nights running ticks Winter Debts by 1.

places.title: Mistlands Maze
places.subtitle: [DEATH] [FEAR]
places.description: Reed-channels braid and vanish; navigation by instinct.
places.flavor: The reeds whisper names you've forgotten. Do not answer.
places.mechanical_hook: Answering a whispered name forces a Resolve roll (DV 5) or the character gains the Condition Fog-Called (compelled to wander toward the sound).

places.title: Boomed Harbor
places.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
places.description: Iron rings in whale-bone posts; controlled access.
places.flavor: The chain was forged from a broken oath. It rattles when liars approach.
places.mechanical_hook: Any character attempting to bluff or deceive while crossing the boom suffers −1 die; the chain's rattle alerts harbor guards.

places.title: Aberderrin Headland
places.subtitle: [DEATH]
places.description: Current rips past wreck timbers in the kelp.
places.flavor: On foggy nights, the drowned signal with lanterns. Never follow.
places.mechanical_hook: Following a drowned-lantern signal leads to a genuine wreck (salvage opportunity) but ticks a relevant danger timer by 1.

places.title: Dolmis Waystation
places.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
places.description: Low isle with fresh water and old weights.
places.flavor: The well is lined with copper. A single dropped coin returns as a blessing.
places.mechanical_hook: Dropping a coin grants a one-time Boon usable at this waystation only, redeemable within one season.

places.title: Thing-Holm
places.subtitle: [JUSTICE]
places.description: Flat islet ringed with stones for speaking and swearing.
places.flavor: The stones have ears; oaths spoken here echo for three tides. The winter oaths are kept here, frozen in a block of ice that never melts.
places.mechanical_hook: An oath sworn here is binding under frost-law; breaking it later automatically advances the Winter Debts timer by 2 instead of the usual 1.

places.title: High Jarl's Seat
places.subtitle: [WEATHER]
places.description: Above fjord, beacon tower glaring out to sea.
places.flavor: The beacon oil is mixed with whale fat. It burns green when a storm is close, blue when the winter debts are called.
places.mechanical_hook: Reading the beacon's color grants the party one free piece of GM-provided foreshadowing about weather or debts due.

places.title: Whale-Road Horizon
places.subtitle: [LEGEND]
places.description: Open water where storms are born and names are made.
places.flavor: Here, the sky meets the sea. Here, the dead meet the living.
places.mechanical_hook: A character who swears a Storm-Oath here gains +1 die on all sea rolls for the remainder of the voyage — but breaking it here inflicts 1 Harm instead of Fatigue.

people_and_factions.title: Net-Wife
people_and_factions.subtitle: [COMMUNITY]
people_and_factions.description: Reads sea like memory, sky like mood; weather-witch in all but name.
people_and_factions.flavor: She ties a knot for every storm she's survived. Her belt has thirty. She is the keeper of the village oath-sticks.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll read the coming weather accurately for the party once, in exchange for help mending nets.
people_and_factions.price: A day's honest labor, or news of the wider coast.

people_and_factions.title: Steersman
people_and_factions.subtitle: [REPUTATION]
people_and_factions.description: Tiller-hand never shakes, even when keel does.
people_and_factions.flavor: His left ear is scarred — he listened too long to a siren's promise. His oath-stick is notched for every life he's lost.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll pilot the party through dangerous waters once, if they don't ask about the scar.
people_and_factions.price: Silence about what he lost, and passage-fare.

people_and_factions.title: Shipwright
people_and_factions.subtitle: [CRAFT]
people_and_factions.description: Pitch on palms, schedule in teeth; knows every plank's story.
people_and_factions.flavor: He names each timber after a dead relative. The keel is his grandmother. The ship's burden is carved into the mast.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll repair a damaged vessel at cost, if the party can name what wood it needs and where it's from.
people_and_factions.price: Materials, and a story about the ship's most recent voyage.

people_and_factions.title: Oar-Master
people_and_factions.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
people_and_factions.description: Sets beat that decides if home is today or never.
people_and_factions.flavor: He drums on a hollowed skull. The rhythm is a prayer to Rorg. The oar-crew's debt is marked on his own arm — notches in the bone.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll grant the party a bench on a fast longship for a voyage, if they row well and ask properly.
people_and_factions.price: A season's labor at the oar, or a favor owed to Rorg.

people_and_factions.title: Mist-Pilot
people_and_factions.subtitle: [STEALTH]
people_and_factions.description: Ghosts boats through marsh lanes; reed-runner with secret paths.
people_and_factions.flavor: He never blinks in fog. Some say he traded his blink for safe passage. His memory-cord is knotted, not notched — the knots are spells.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll guide the party through the Mistlands Maze safely, once, if they don't ask what he traded.
people_and_factions.price: A dried eel skin token, or a secret kept from the sea.

people_and_factions.title: Skald
people_and_factions.subtitle: [JUSTICE] [SOCIAL]
people_and_factions.description: Verses buy silence, start fights, end them; law in rhyme.
people_and_factions.flavor: Her tongue is forked — she can praise and curse in the same breath. She is the only one who can reshape a frost-bound oath — by composing a new verse that changes the meaning of a mark.
people_and_factions.debt: She'll compose a verse to reshape a named oath's meaning, once, if the request is honest.
people_and_factions.price: A true story worthy of verse, told without embellishment.

people_and_factions.title: Shield-Band
people_and_factions.subtitle: [COMBAT]
people_and_factions.description: Cousins fine with coin, better with cattle.
people_and_factions.flavor: They sharpen their swords on runestones. The sparks tell fortunes. Their oath-stick is shared — each mark is a blood debt owed to the band.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll fight alongside the party for one engagement, if the cause aligns with a family grudge.
people_and_factions.price: A cut of any plunder, and future favor owed to the band.

people_and_factions.title: Foster-Son
people_and_factions.subtitle: [POLITICS]
people_and_factions.description: Southern coast birth; speaks both laws and subtext.
people_and_factions.flavor: He wears two brooches — one iron, one bone. Neither is his true allegiance. He carries two oath-sticks — one for the Linn, one for the lowlands.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll translate or broker between Linn and southern factions, once, if treated as an equal by both.
people_and_factions.price: Information split evenly between both sides he serves.

people_and_factions.title: Thing-Speaker
people_and_factions.subtitle: [JUSTICE]
people_and_factions.description: Makes war into lawsuit, lawsuit into lunch.
people_and_factions.flavor: He carries a water-timer that runs on meltwater. When it runs out, so does your patience. He interprets the winter debts for those who cannot read ice.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll interpret a frost-bound oath's true terms, once, for anyone willing to sit through the full proceeding.
people_and_factions.price: Patience, and a fee paid to the Thing.

people_and_factions.title: Sea-Queen's Hand
people_and_factions.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
people_and_factions.description: Envoy with seal-bag and sword-belt; queen's will made manifest.
people_and_factions.flavor: He never draws his blade. The threat is enough. His oath-stick is branded with the queen's mark — a seal that cannot be forged.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll grant a harbor-mark or writ on the Queen's authority, once, for genuine service rendered.
people_and_factions.price: Loyalty demonstrated publicly, and future obligation to the crown.

people_and_factions.title: Sea-Queen
people_and_factions.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
people_and_factions.description: Crown of hammered silver, eyes for weather and law.
people_and_factions.flavor: She lost an eye to a storm — or to a spy. She won't say which. She is the only one who can order the winter debts spoken.
people_and_factions.debt: She grants audience rarely, but her word bends sea-law when she chooses to speak it.
people_and_factions.price: A service that only a trusted outsider could perform.

people_and_factions.title: High Jarl
people_and_factions.subtitle: [REPUTATION]
people_and_factions.description: First among raids, last to boast; paramount over strands.
people_and_factions.flavor: His beard is braided with silver from every ship he's taken. His oath-stick is a whale's rib — too long for anyone else to carry.
people_and_factions.debt: He owes the moot-holders a decision on a season's raid; helping him decide grants standing.
people_and_factions.price: Public backing for whichever course you help him choose.

people_and_factions.title: Volva of Mist
people_and_factions.subtitle: [LEGEND]
people_and_factions.description: Oath-reader whose nod stills surf; seer of tides and truth.
people_and_factions.flavor: She speaks once a year. The rest of the time, she listens to the fog. She reads the frost-bound oaths by touch — her fingers are scarred from counting.
people_and_factions.debt: Her yearly words are prophecy — genuine, cryptic, and binding on those who hear them.
people_and_factions.price: A memory, freely given, in trade for a glimpse of fate.

complications.title: Black Squall
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER]
complications.description: Drops from clear band; oars or prayers — pick one.
complications.flavor: The wind screams a name. Listen carefully — it might be yours. Rorg is testing your courage.
complications.mechanical_hook: Weather the squall with an Endurance or Boating roll (DV 4); a Miss inflicts 1 Fatigue on the crew and ticks Winter Debts by 1 if a Storm-Oath was recently broken nearby.

complications.title: Fogfall
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER] [FEAR]
complications.description: Sound travels, sight does not; friend and reef trade places.
complications.flavor: You hear oars. Then you don't. Then they're behind you. The drowned are rowing.
complications.mechanical_hook: Navigation becomes Desperate until the fog clears; a character who calls out for reassurance risks the Mistlands Maze's whispering effect.

complications.title: Boom Lift
complications.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
complications.description: Harbor chain rises; schedules drown in harbor mouth.
complications.flavor: The chain's links are inscribed with names of those who carry weight. Each one rattles differently. Your name is on one.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party is delayed one segment on any relevant timer, and the harbor guard now knows their names and business.

complications.title: Levy Clash
complications.subtitle: [POLITICS] [COMBAT]
complications.description: Viterra's wardens arrive with polite spears.
complications.flavor: They carry a writ stamped with the queen's seal. The seal is still wet. The winter ice says the queen is owed three ships.
complications.mechanical_hook: Resolving the levy peacefully requires a Sway roll (DV 5); failure escalates to a Cap 2 armed confrontation.

complications.title: Keel-Rot Rumor
complications.subtitle: [DISASTER]
complications.description: Crews beach mid-voyage; trust in timber fails.
complications.flavor: The rot smells sweet — too sweet. Someone poisoned the tar. The ship's mark is missing.
complications.mechanical_hook: Investigating the sabotage grants a genuine lead on the saboteur (GM's choice); ignoring it risks the vessel becoming unseaworthy mid-journey.

complications.title: Feud Token
complications.subtitle: [SOCIAL] [DEBT]
complications.description: Raid becomes wedding… or funeral; oath-debt called due.
complications.flavor: A bronze ring arrives on an arrow. The meaning is clear. The ice shows the mark.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party must choose a side or broker peace via a Skald or Thing-Speaker (Sway DV 5); refusal starts a Feud Spiral timer against a random ally.

complications.title: Oath Matured
complications.subtitle: [SOCIAL] [DEBT]
complications.description: Verse sworn last winter comes due today.
complications.flavor: The skald clears her throat. The room goes cold. The ice in the Thing-Holm cracks.
complications.mechanical_hook: A character who swore an oath earlier in the campaign must now fulfill it or take the mechanical Winter Debts penalty in full.

complications.title: Mistlands Miscount
complications.subtitle: [DEATH]
complications.flavor: The fog lifts to reveal a different shore. Your charts are now lies. The cargo's mark is blank — someone erased it.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party loses 1 Supply of cargo and must re-navigate from an unknown position (Wits+Lore, DV 5, to reorient).

complications.title: Aberderrin Race
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER]
complications.description: Contrary currents split flotilla; half late, half lost.
complications.flavor: The water churns like a dying man. Something beneath is feeding. The sea remembers a new debt.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party's vessel is separated from any escort or allied ship for the remainder of the voyage unless a Boating roll (DV 5) succeeds.

complications.title: Southron Fire-Pots
complications.subtitle: [COMBAT]
complications.description: Night-run turns to daylight; surprise ashore.
complications.flavor: Pots shatter on the deck. The fire burns blue — alchemical. Rorg laughs. The raid's memory is now fire-scarred.
complications.mechanical_hook: Any stealth approach is immediately voided; combat begins at a disadvantageous range band.

complications.title: Thing Injunction
complications.subtitle: [JUSTICE]
complications.description: No sailing till grievance heard (hours? days?).
complications.flavor: The Thing-Speaker smiles. He has all the time in the world. The winter oath is frozen — no one can leave until it thaws.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party cannot depart the settlement until the grievance is resolved, one way or another — treat as a forced scene.

complications.title: General Muster
complications.subtitle: [AUTHORITY] [COMBAT]
complications.description: Horns on every headland; all bays become spears.
complications.flavor: The war fleet assembles. Your ship is the smallest. Adar is watching. He counts the oaths.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party is conscripted into the muster unless they can produce a valid exemption (a writ, a Frost Mark cleared, or a jarl's favor).

complications.title: Ground-Sea
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER] [DEATH]
complications.description: Long, blind swell rolls under; steering lies.
complications.flavor: The swell has a rhythm — two short, one long. A signal from below. The drowned are voting.
complications.mechanical_hook: A character who recognizes the rhythm (Wits+Lore, DV 5) can avoid the worst of the swell; failure inflicts 1 Harm and ticks a relevant danger timer.

rewards.title: Harbor-Mark
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Dock without levy in named strand (once).
rewards.flavor: The mark is a notch cut in a bone. Match it to the harbor post. The notch must be cut by the harbor master's own knife.
rewards.curse_cost: The mark works only in the one strand it was cut for, and only once.

rewards.title: Oar-Share
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Claim two benches on a fast longship for a season.
rewards.flavor: The oars are carved with your name. Row well, or they'll be recarved. The oar itself is the promise.
rewards.curse_cost: Failing to row when called upon voids the share and marks the holder as an oath-breaker.

rewards.title: Pilot's Token
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.flavor: The token is a dried eel skin. Keep it dry. The pilot's memory-cord is knotted in the same pattern.
rewards.curse_cost: If the token gets wet, the pilot's guidance is voided mid-journey.

rewards.title: Wharf-Right
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Dolmis waystation loading priority; first ashore.
rewards.flavor: The harbormaster frowns but steps aside. Your name is now on a list.
rewards.curse_cost: Being 'on the list' means the harbormaster's rivals now also know who you are.

rewards.title: Salvage Claim
rewards.subtitle: [TRADE]
rewards.flavor: You must name each piece before touching it. The wrong word forfeits the claim. Say it wrong twice, and the tide takes the whole pile back.
rewards.curse_cost: Misnaming a piece forfeits that piece's claim permanently, and may draw the attention of whoever it truly belonged to.

rewards.title: Thing Ruling
rewards.subtitle: [JUSTICE]
rewards.description: Verdict in your favor that travels with you.
rewards.flavor: The verdict is carved on a whale-rib. Carry it as a shield. The winter ice will not speak for the same dispute twice.
rewards.curse_cost: The ruling cannot be invoked twice for the same dispute — once spent, it is spent.

rewards.title: Raid-Truce
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [SOCIAL]
rewards.description: Immunity in named bay for one market day.
rewards.flavor: A white banner on your mast. No one will attack — openly. Cut the banner rope, and every eye on the water knows it before you've coiled it.
rewards.curse_cost: The truce only protects against open attack; it does nothing against subtler harm.

rewards.title: Foster-Bond
rewards.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
rewards.description: Guest-kin by jarl's house; hospitality guaranteed.
rewards.flavor: You share a cup with the jarl. The cup is silver. The promise is iron. The winter ice bears a new mark — for both of you.
rewards.curse_cost: The bond obligates the party to the jarl's household in turn, someday, in a manner of the jarl's choosing.

rewards.title: Herring Allotment
rewards.subtitle: [TRADE]
rewards.description: Priority barrels when the run hits; silver in season.
rewards.flavor: The barrels are sealed with your mark. Break one to test quality; the hoop remembers whose knife did it.
rewards.curse_cost: The allotment lasts only one season and must be renewed through continued good standing.

rewards.title: Escort Writ
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [COMBAT]
rewards.description: Eight shields and wolf-banner from cape to cape.
rewards.flavor: The shields are painted with a wolf's head. They die before you do. Their oath is their swords — notched for every oath kept.
rewards.curse_cost: The escort's loyalty is to the writ, not to you personally — if the writ is revoked, so is their protection, mid-journey if need be.

rewards.title: Queen's Audience
rewards.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
rewards.description: Whisper exits as policy; sea-law bends.
rewards.flavor: The Queen's hand writes your words on vellum. The ink is her blood. The winter ice will record the audience — but not the words.
rewards.curse_cost: What you ask for becomes policy — for everyone, not just you, and policy can be reversed by rivals with better arguments.

rewards.title: High Jarl's Pennon
rewards.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
rewards.description: Levies open booms and mouths when it flies.
rewards.flavor: The pennon is torn from a captured ship. Fly it proudly — or else. Whoever lost the mast it came from is still counting who owns the wind now.
rewards.curse_cost: Flying the pennon falsely, or losing it, brings the High Jarl's wrath down on the bearer directly.

rewards.title: Storm-Oath Clause
rewards.subtitle: [AUTHORITY] [MAGIC]
rewards.description: Temporary exception to any sea-law, sealed.
rewards.flavor: The clause is whispered, never written. The sea hears and obeys — once. The winter ice cannot record a whisper, but Rorg has no trouble keeping count.
rewards.curse_cost: Rorg's memory of the favor owed is long, and his idea of an appropriate repayment rarely matches the asker's.

quick_use_notes.draw_rules: Draw until you have all four suits: Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 → 4, 6–10 → 6, J/Q/K → 8, A → 10).
quick_use_notes.diamonds: Diamonds are codified outcomes (rights/tokens/escorts) that change position rather than call for a roll.
quick_use_notes.ace_rule: If any Ace appears, echo sea-omens — horns on wind, white horses on swell, verse unfinished until landfall, the ice cracking with memory.

additional_features.frost_mark_mechanics: Every favor or gift from a Linn creates a Frost Mark — a 4-segment timer. When full, the community demands service (raid, story, labor). Refusal imposes −1 die on social rolls until resolved.
additional_features.season_turn: The GM may spend 3 Story Beats to change the season. Spring: foraging/healing +1; Summer: combat/sailing +1; Autumn: social/legal +1; Winter: survival Desperate, Frost Marks clear more easily.
temple_pressure_events: **Grain Fleet Arrives.** Temple ships bring cheap grain; prices drop, but old shrine offerings are neglected. Tick Temple Pressure +1.
**Synod Court Opens.** A judge hears disputes; feuds may be settled with penance instead of blood-silver. Shrine-devout suffer −1 Position here.
**Bell Tower Consecrated.** A bronze bell rings nine times at dawn; old shrine bells fall silent. Temple-leaning gain +1 die on faith actions.
**Schoolmaster Arrives.** Children learn Temple script; oral traditions called superstition. Next generation gains +1 Temple Devotion.
**Bishop's Progress.** A high cleric tours the coast. Begin a Bishop's Favor [4] timer; if it fills, he demands a public oath.
**Iconoclasm.** Zealots burn a seastack shrine. Shrine-devout gain a Vengeance Oath String; weather hazards worsen for 1d4 days.

faith_devotion_spectrum.description: Linn faith ranges from shrine-devout (−3) to Temple-favored (+3). Most are mixed. Use the following overlays:

bands.-3_to_-2: Shrine-Favored: +1 die on patron rites or shrine diplomacy; −1 Position in Temple-dominated venues.
bands.-1_to_+1: Bridge-Walker: No innate bonus; can qualify for Ambassador Status.
bands.+2_to_+3: Temple-Favored: +1 die on Temple rites or court scenes; −1 Position in shrine strongholds.

faith_devotion_spectrum.synthesis_tokens: When players successfully blend shrine and Temple practices, gain a Synthesis Token (max 2). Spend to: improve Position on a faith action by one step, gain +1 die on diplomacy between factions, or declare safe passage.
faith_devotion_spectrum.dual_oaths: A character swearing both to shrine and Temple must choose which faith is offended on a roll with 1s. Refusing to choose marks Spiritual Conflict (−1 die to faith actions until resolved).
faith_devotion_spectrum.contamination: Performing rites in the 'wrong' space may apply a Contamination Token. Clear with downtime or convert to XP (1 Token = 1 XP toward a faith-aligned talent).

saga_system.description: The Saga system tracks legendary deeds. Each crew has a Saga Reputation track (1–6).
saga_system.earning: Award Saga Points for epic victories, impossible feats, honor-keeping, legendary sacrifices, or story-shaping decisions. 1–2 points per deed.

benefits.1-2: Local Heroes: once per scene, improve Position by one step when defending home or kin.
benefits.3-4: Regional Champions: once per session, invoke a past deed for +1 die on a relevant roll.
benefits.5-6: Living Legends: once per session, treat any Controlled Position as Dominant for a single action.

saga_system.complications: Fame brings rivals, expectations, and Saga Debts. The GM may introduce rival challenges, expectation burdens, or target status.

lore_echoes.title: The Draugr's Silver
lore_echoes.description: A jarl died with an unpaid oath and rose as a draugr. He demanded his wife settle the tally with blood or battle. She armed his corpse and sent him to fight a draugr-lord in the Direwood. He lost, but the tally was paid. The story teaches that the dead do not wait for payment—they collect.

lore_echoes.title: The Shield That Forgot
lore_echoes.description: A warrior named Astrid lost her shield, which held her life's memories. Without it, she forgot her name. She found a black river stone carved with the rune Uruz, which restored a fragment of her memory—enough to remember her name, but not all of her past. The story reminds that names are oaths owed to the people who speak them.

lore_echoes.title: The Ninth Rune
lore_echoes.description: A skald sought the ninth rune—the rune of grief for the dead. He found a standing stone in the Mistland that showed the name of his drowned son. He learned that the ninth rune is not carved; it is witnessed. Speaking the name of the dead is enough to honor them, but only once a year.

lore_echoes.title: The Mist-Walker's Gift
lore_echoes.description: A young woman entered the Mistland to find her father, who had become part of the fog. The fog takes memories; to recover them, one must tell a story the fog has never heard. Nine stories bought her father's return. The Mistland is a tally—every breath is an entry.

lore_echoes.title: The Valewood Hunt
lore_echoes.description: A warrior boasted he would spend a night in the Valewood and bring back a relic. He took a crown from a phasing city and was hunted by its queen. He escaped by leaving the crown behind. The Valewood shows you what you fear—and then what you forgot.

lore_echoes.title: The Ship That Sailed Over Land
lore_echoes.description: An old longship, the Fjord-Wyrm, could no longer float. Rather than burn it, a shipwright returned it to the forest, where it became soil and grew new trees. The story teaches that a ship is a promise; to destroy it is to break an oath. It must be transformed.

lore_echoes.title: The Skald Who Lost Her Tongue
lore_echoes.description: A rival cut out the tongue of a skald named Signy. She traded her blood to a selkie for a new tongue, which could speak a person's true name—and cause them to forget their own story. A tongue is a weapon; a whisper is sharper.

lore_echoes.title: The Hearth That Would Not Die
lore_echoes.description: A longhouse burned, but the hearth stone remained. The family swore new oaths before it to keep the fire alive. A hearth is a witness; forget the oaths, and the hearth goes cold.

lore_echoes.title: The Oath of the Unsung Dead
lore_echoes.description: A jarl cut a tree from the Direwood without offering a story. His descendants owed three hundred stories to the forest. The Direwood remembers; the price is paid in stories, never coin.

lore_echoes.title: The Ninth
lore_echoes.description: In any longhouse, the ninth horn blown at a feast summons the Hollow. The wise stop at eight. Those who blow the ninth see a pale figure at the high table—Adar, checking his oath-stick. The ninth is the unwitnessed death, the debt that can never be paid.

superstitions.name: Bread to the Wake
superstitions.effect: Toss a crust over the gunwale before a voyage. Ignore the first Black Squall penalty.

superstitions.name: Knot the Oar
superstitions.effect: Tie a single knot in your oar's leather grip. Cancel Keel-Rot Rumor or take −1 die on your next rowing check (your choice).

superstitions.name: Name to the Deep
superstitions.effect: Whisper a dead enemy's name into the tide. Gain +1 Effect against his kin for the scene, but mark Obligation to the Sea-Queen.

superstitions.name: Drink to the Storm
superstitions.effect: Pour a cup of mead into the sea before a raid. Rorg will grant favorable winds — but he will also expect a share of the plunder.

decline_and_patronage: Among the Linn, power flows through oaths, kinship, and the spoken word — and through the marks carved in ice. Jarls maintain authority through successful raids and wise judgments, while skalds wield influence through their ability to immortalize deeds in verse — or damn names through satire. The Sea-Queen holds sway over the coastlands, but her rule depends on the respect of the High Jarl and the Thing-speakers who interpret ancient laws. And beneath all of them lies the frost-bound memory — the carved word, not the written one. Patronage here is as brittle as winter ice: a jarl's favor can melt with a broken oath, a skald's blessing can turn to curse with a single false verse. To seek a patron among the Linn is to accept that your name will be carved — and that carving can never be fully erased. The Temple of Light offers a different kind of weight: absolution, not memory; forgiveness, not obligation. But the Linn know that a debt forgiven is still a debt owed. The frost remembers. The sea remembers. And the Hollow is patient.

minor_complications: **Exposure:** Your actions draw unwanted attention from **jarls or Thing-speakers**.
**Noise:** Sounds of your actions alert nearby **watchmen or shield-bands**.
**Trace:** Evidence of your passage marks your route for **trackers or rival clans**.
**Delay:** A brief but meaningful setback costs you **time or favorable weather**.
**Supply Strain:** Mark +1 segment on a relevant **resource timer**.
moderate_setbacks: **Alarm Raised:** **Sea-Queen's Hand or High Jarl's retinue** becomes aware and begins responding.
**Position Lost:** You lose advantageous ground/cover/stealth due to **fog or tide shift**.
**Foe Appears:** A **rival clan's raiders or Temple zealots** arrives on scene.
**Gear Trouble:** A piece of equipment becomes **Compromised/Neglected**.
**Lock/Barrier:** A simple obstacle now requires a test to overcome.
serious_trouble: **Reinforcements:** Additional **shield-bands, Temple guards, or war-fleet** arrive.
**Key Gear Breaks:** A crucial tool/weapon becomes temporarily unusable.
**Major Twist:** The situation fundamentally changes - **oath is called due/raid-truce broken/frost-mark claimed**.
**Rail Tick:** Advance a relevant campaign/front timer by 1 segment.
major_turns: **Trap Springs:** A prepared danger activates with full effect.
**Authority Arrival:** **High Jarl, Sea-Queen, or Volva of Mist** intervenes.
**Scene Shift:** The environment changes dramatically - **storm breaks/fog descends/ice cracks**.
**Patron Omen:** Divine/arcane forces take notice - **omen appears/blessing lost/curse manifests**.
**Narrative Pivot:** The story takes an unexpected turn that reframes objectives.
region_specific: **Linn (Skerries & Storm-Oaths):** A horn is blown nine times; a ship appears on the horizon that no one recognizes; the ice cracks with a voice.
**Linn (Oaths & Law):** An oath is called due; a Thing-Speaker challenges your testimony; a Frost Mark is claimed against you.
**Linn (Sea & Weather):** A squall rises with no warning; the tide turns three bells early; a white bear is seen on the ice.
**Linn (The Temple Crusade):** A bell tolls from a newly consecrated tower; a bishop demands an oath of loyalty; a shrine is burned in the night.

boss_archetypes.name: The Draugr Jarl
boss_archetypes.description: A dead jarl whose oath was never fulfilled. He rises when the ninth bell tolls, demanding a blood-price paid in stories.
cracks: Fulfill the oath he swore in life
Convince the Thing-Speaker to record a new verdict
Offer a memory heavy enough to satisfy the frost

boss_archetypes.name: The Temple Bishop
boss_archetypes.description: A southern prelate determined to convert the Linn, by grain, by law, or by fire.
cracks: Expose a corruption in his synod court
Persuade a converted jarl to switch sides
Restore a shrine he ordered burned

boss_archetypes.name: The Mist-Walker
boss_archetypes.description: A Linn who entered the Mistlands without an offering and became part of the fog.
cracks: Tell the Mist-Walker a story it has never heard

boss_archetypes.name: The Valewood Queen
boss_archetypes.description: A queen of a phasing city in the Valewood, whose crown was stolen and whose attention is jealous.
cracks: Allow a willing sacrifice to take the queen's place

boss_archetypes.name: The Sea-Queen's Rival
boss_archetypes.description: A jarl who has gathered enough ships and oaths to challenge the Sea-Queen's law.
cracks: Broker a truce between the two
Sway the Thing-Speaker to the queen's side

encounter_seeds.title: The Draugr's Silver
encounter_seeds.description: A Linn jarl's corpse has risen, demanding payment for an oath unfulfilled. The party must find the weregild and offer it before the draugr kills again.

encounter_seeds.title: The Shield That Forgot
encounter_seeds.description: A Linn warrior has lost her shield—and her name. She remembers only that she swore an oath to a dead jarl. The party must help her find the shield or a new memory before she is forgotten.

encounter_seeds.title: The Mist-Walker's Gift
encounter_seeds.description: A Linn chieftain's son walked into the Mistland three days ago. The party must find him, but the fog takes memories every hour. They must tell stories to the fog to keep their own names—and to buy the son's freedom.

encounter_seeds.title: The Valewood Hunt
encounter_seeds.description: A Linn warrior took a bronze crown from a phasing city. Now the queen walks behind him. The party must find the city and return the crown before the queen takes more than a name.

encounter_seeds.title: The Ship That Sailed Over Land
encounter_seeds.description: A Linn jarl inherited a longship that has been in his family for six generations. The ship is rotting. If he burns it, the ancestors will curse him. The party must help him return the ship to the forest—or convince the forest to accept it.

being_looked_at.name: Counter-Phobia
being_looked_at.summary:
Do not write the Linn as bold. Write them as a people in the grip of a dread they refuse to be governed by, who have decided that the only tolerable relationship with the thing that watches is to walk straight at it in front of witnesses.

Their real horror is the unwitnessed death: going into the water in bad weather with nobody on the shore, coming to nothing, and no one afterward able to say it happened. Set against that, being noticed by something at the high table is the lesser of two terrors, and the Linn have organized an entire culture around always choosing the lesser one at speed. The boast comes before the deed and not after — not swagger, but a door locked behind them.

The sagas give this away if you read them closely. They are not much interested in the fight. They dwell, at length and in detail, on the hour before it: the weather, who was in the hall, what a man's hands were doing. That is the part the Linn find worth recording, because that is the part that was hard.
being_looked_at.at_the_table: Linn characters gain real benefit from acting in front of witnesses and lose standing for quiet successes, however sensible — a Linn who solves a problem by stealth has not solved it. But play the cost honestly: they are afraid, visibly, before they commit, and a Linn player who never shows the fear is playing a different people. The courage is in the going, not in the absence of dread.
